case.paper_title: Human Capital and Development Accounting: New Evidence from Wage Gains at Migration
case.focal_claim: ... immigrants who have never been to high school gain ... more on migration to the United States than immigrants with a college degree (p. 682.)
case.hypothesis: Immigrants with no high school exposure have larger wage gains from their last home-country job to their U.S. job than immigrants with a college degree.

tasks_info.task_instruction: In Task 1, the analyst was asked to conduct the analysis without any restrictions.
tasks_info.task_goal: Test whether the focal claim is supported.

tasks_info.task_instruction: You should use the pooled sample of immigrants from poor countries in the NIS (New Immigrant Survey) and the Migration Projects, including Mexico. You should not control for sector: agriculture/nonagriculture, and region i.e. whether an immigrant grew up in a rural or an urban area.
tasks_info.task_goal: Produce one statistical result comparable to the original paper's focal result.

datasets.notes: The dataset has complete non-null entries for all 12 columns. Adjusted home wages have extreme values, with lastHomeWageAdjusted max approximately 9,504,020.70, motivating a robust-estimation candidate without deleting observations. No GDP-per-worker variable or explicit NIS/Migration Projects source indicator is available in the file.

reference_specification.variable_construction: Compute log_wage_gain as log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted). conclusion_rule.expected_direction: The no_high_school wage-gain coefficient relative to college_degree is positive.
conclusion_rule.statistical_threshold: p < 0.05 describes strong statistical evidence; p >= 0.05 with an expected-direction estimate remains weak directional support.
conclusion_rule.support_rule: Support when the focal point estimate or pattern is in the expected direction. Opposite requires affirmative evidence of a material effect in the contrary direction; an opposite-signed estimate alone is inconclusive. A non-significant result in the expected direction remains weak directional support.

evidence.paper: The focal claim appears on p. 682: immigrants who have never been to high school gain more on migration to the United States than immigrants with a college degree. The paper summary states that wage gains are calculated by comparing immigrants' pre- and post-migration hourly wages adjusted to U.S. dollars/PPP and that less educated workers have larger migration wage gains.

uncertainties: The exact original table/regression specification for p. 682 is not fully available from the summarized PDF text, so the OLS adjusted anchor uses verified variables and prior paper-described wage-gain construction.
The paper's exact standard-error method for this focal education comparison is not_stated in the readable summary.

plan.path_summary: Estimate the focal no-high-school versus college-degree contrast in individual log wage gains using Huber robust linear regression. Task1 uses the unrestricted adjusted specification with verified demographic, country, and timing controls; Task2 uses the required pooled poor-country sample including Mexico and no sector or rural/urban region controls.

path_signature.sample_restriction: Use authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx; Task2 treats it as the pooled poor-country NIS/Migration Projects sample including Mexico; require positive adjusted wages and nonmissing required variables.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion on required raw and constructed variables; drop nonpositive adjusted wages for log transformation.
path_signature.variable_construction: Compute log_wage_gain as log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted); categorize edyrs into no_high_school <=8, some_high_school 9-11, high_school 12, some_college 13-15, college_degree >=16; Task1 also constructs age_home_job and age_home_job_sq.
path_signature.inference_rule: A positive no_high_school coefficient relative to college_degree is support; p < 0.05 indicates strong statistical evidence and p >= 0.05 with a positive estimate is weak directional support. A negative estimate is inconclusive unless p < 0.05 and the confidence interval excludes zero in the negative direction.

analysis_path.path_description: Run Huber robust linear regression of individual log wage gain on education groups, using college degree as the reference and estimating the no-high-school contrast while adjusting for country, sex, age at last home job, squared age, and last home/U.S. job years.
preprocessing_steps: Load data/wage_gain_table.xlsx.
Verify required columns: edyrs, yearLastHomeJob, yearLastUsJob, sex, yrborn, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWageAdjusted, country.
Report starting rows.
Drop rows missing required raw columns and report removals.
Keep rows with lastHomeWageAdjusted > 0 and lastUsWageAdjusted > 0 and report removals.
Compute log_wage_gain = log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted).
Construct edu_group from edyrs with no_high_school <=8, some_high_school 9-11, high_school 12, some_college 13-15, college_degree >=16.
Construct age_home_job = yearLastHomeJob - yrborn and age_home_job_sq = age_home_job squared.
Drop rows with missing or nonfinite constructed variables and report removals.
Set college_degree as the education reference category and preserve intermediate education groups.
Fit robust linear model log_wage_gain on edu_group, country indicators, sex indicators, age_home_job, age_home_job_sq, yearLastHomeJob, and yearLastUsJob using HuberT weights.

Report the focal no_high_school versus college_degree coefficient, standard error, z statistic, p value, approximate 95% confidence interval, exponentiated percent difference, sample flow, and conclusion class.

key_choices.main_predictor_measure: Categorical education group from edyrs, with no_high_school defined as edyrs <= 8 and college_degree as edyrs >= 16
key_choices.sample_restriction: Authorized dataset rows with nonmissing required variables and positive adjusted home and U.S. wages.
key_choices.outlier_rule: No trimming or deletion of outliers; Huber robust estimation downweights observations with large residuals.
key_choices.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion on required raw and constructed variables.
key_choices.data_processing: Log-transform wage ratio through differenced logs; recode education years into five groups; create age at last home job and squared age; use categorical indicators for country and sex.
key_choices.model_choice: Huber robust linear regression fit with statsmodels RLM and HuberT norm.
key_choices.inference_rule: An estimate in the expected positive direction is support; it is strong support when p < 0.05 and weak or directional support otherwise. Opposite requires p < 0.05 and an approximate 95% confidence interval excluding zero in the contrary direction.

models.formula: log_wage_gain ~ C(edu_group, Treatment(reference='college_degree')) + C(country) + C(sex) + age_home_job + age_home_job_sq + yearLastHomeJob + yearLastUsJob
models.planned_estimation: Robust-regression coefficient for no_high_school relative to college_degree in log_wage_gain
models.inference_criteria: A positive focal coefficient supports the claim; p < 0.05 describes strong statistical evidence, while p >= 0.05 with a positive estimate is weak directional support. An opposite negative conclusion requires affirmative evidence: p < 0.05 and confidence interval below zero.
models.qualification: The paper focal estimand is an individual wage-gain education contrast. The dataset contains extreme adjusted wage values, especially lastHomeWageAdjusted, so Huber robust regression is a defensible robustness model that preserves the full sample and focal contrast while reducing sensitivity to outlying residuals.

outcome.variable_construction: np.log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - np.log(lastHomeWageAdjusted), after requiring both adjusted wages to be positive.
outcome.missing_data_handling: Rows with missing or nonfinite constructed log_wage_gain are dropped and reported in sample flow.
outcome.qualification: The paper studies wage gains on migration using adjusted home and U.S. wages; log differences directly operationalize proportional wage gains.

method_justification.claim_alignment: Both tasks estimate whether the wage gain from migration is larger for immigrants with no high school exposure than for immigrants with college degrees, exactly matching the focal claim's education contrast.
method_justification.dataset_alignment: Both tasks use only the authorized original dataset data/wage_gain_table.xlsx. Task2 treats the supplied file as the pooled poor-country NIS/Migration Projects sample including Mexico and applies no country filter.
method_justification.method_reason: Log wage gain is aligned with proportional wage-gain comparisons. Huber robust regression is appropriate because the dataset contains extreme adjusted wage values, and it offers a robustness check that retains observations while reducing outlier sensitivity. Task1 uses verified demographic, country, and timing controls under the unrestricted instruction. Task2 uses no controls, satisfying the prohibition on sector and rural/urban region controls.
method_justification.novelty_reason: Shared Memory already contains adjusted/unadjusted OLS, median quantile regression, and trimmed OLS paths. This path changes only the model family to Huber robust M-estimation while preserving outcome, contrast, sample, and Task2 restrictions.

self_check.self_check_note: The plan keeps the focal wage-gain education contrast and authorized dataset. It differs from all prior shared-memory paths by using Huber robust regression rather than OLS, quantile regression, or trimming. Both scripts were written and read back; referenced columns exist in the inspected dataset.

execution_directives.instructions: Execute Task1 and Task2 using the authorized original dataset and the candidate-specific entry scripts. Do not redesign the analyses during execution.

debugging_rule.repair_scope: Fix dependency, import, file path, or output serialization issues only; do not change the dataset, focal variables, sample restrictions, model family, controls, or inference rule.

execution_directives.comparison_metrics: For each task, report the no_high_school versus college_degree robust log-wage-gain coefficient, standard error, p-value, approximate 95% confidence interval, exponentiated percent difference, final analytic sample size, sample-flow removals, and conclusion class.
